label: DAY 24
title: AI plays my elevator game. The obvious bot froze in 998 of 1,000 games.

lines.text: I've been waiting in this lobby forever.
Sorry. My elevator bot froze. In 998 of 1,000 games.

scenes.title: My game: Lift Rush

items.text: Doors open to drop or pick up
Score: ticks until you get off

lines.text: Hold on. You made an elevator game?

lines: Ten floors, one car, six people max.
Bots only choose up or down. Fewer ticks waiting wins.

scenes.title: 5 AI bots

items.text: Lobby: Nearest, parks in the lobby

lines: Random, and Nearest, which goes to the closest call.
Sweep keeps going one way, then turns around.
Oldest serves whoever waited longest. Lobby parks downstairs.

scenes.title: Avg ticks per trip, 1,000 games each
Why Nearest froze
log: they can't fit, so it waits for them
lines: It filled up. The closest call was the people right outside the door.
They can't fit. So it waits for them. Forever.
Lobby has the same flaw. It froze 998 times too.

lines.text: Same game, Sweep. It just keeps moving.
By the end, Sweep dropped off 237 people. Nearest, 9.

scenes.title: The fix: Nearest+, 1,000 games
lines: I did. When it's full, it ignores the people waiting.
Now it averages 20.6 ticks. Almost a tie.

scenes.title: People who waited 60+ ticks
lines: But count the people who waited over sixty ticks.

lines.text: Nearest plus: 845. Sweep: 140. Six times more.

scenes.title: Who waited longer
log: $ avg wait for pickup, by floor
lines: It keeps grabbing the close calls. The top floors wait.
Sweep is the classic elevator algorithm. Disk scheduling uses it too.

scenes.text: The obvious bot froze. The boring one won.
scenes.sub: What elevator rule should I try next?
lines: What elevator rule should I test next? Tell me in the comments.
